mainTopic: The מלאכה of בונה on שבת: the minimum amount, setting stones, and whether chiseling is בונה or מכה בפטיש
overview: The משנה teaches that one who builds on שבת is liable for even a tiny amount (כל שהוא). The same is true of chiseling, the final hammer blow (מכה בפטיש), and drilling, because any מלאכה whose result lasts makes one liable. The גמרא asks what use a tiny building could have. After two examples are rejected, it settles on sealing a small hole, which parallels filling a worm hole in a משכן beam with lead. Next, שמואל rules that setting a stone in place is building. The גמרא answers a challenge to him by explaining that each row of a wall has its own requirement: dirt for the bottom row, mortar for the middle row, and mere placement for the top row. רב and שמואל then argue whether chiseling, making a hole in a chicken coop, and putting a pin in a hoe handle count as בונה or מכה בפטיש, and the גמרא explains why all three cases are needed. רבי יוחנן answers with a hand gesture that chiseling is מכה בפטיש. The גמרא reads the משנה to fit his answer, and then begins a proof that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: building any amount makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how much one must build to be liable. It answers that any amount (כל שהוא) is enough, and the same is true for chiseling, hammering, and drilling.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who builds — how much must he build to be liable? One who builds any amount, and one who chisels, and one who strikes with a hammer or an adze, and one who drills any amount — is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the topic of בונה on שבת. It rules that there is no minimum size: even a tiny bit of building makes one חייב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many מלאכות have a minimum amount (a שיעור) before one is liable. Here the משנה says building has no such minimum. It lists related acts that also count at any size: chiseling stone, the final hammer blow (מכה בפטיש), working with an adze, and drilling a hole.

keyTerms.meaning: One who builds — the מלאכה of בונה
Any amount at all; no minimum size
Striking with a hammer — the final finishing blow

steps.whyThisMatters: This 'any amount' ruling is what triggers the entire גמרא that follows: what use is a tiny building?

phrases.english: MISHNAH: One who builds,
how much must he build to be liable?
One who builds any amount,
and one who chisels, and one who strikes with a hammer or with an adze,
one who drills any amount — is liable.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Building, chiseling, final hammering, and drilling make one liable at any size, with no minimum amount.

steps.title: The general rule: lasting work makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a general principle: anyone who does a מלאכה whose result lasts is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the principle: anyone who does a מלאכה, and his work lasts on שבת — is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up its list with a general rule (זה הכלל). The key test is whether the work you did stays in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule explains why even a tiny act counts: what matters is that the result is lasting, not that it is large. Work that falls apart right away does not make one liable.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the forbidden categories of creative work on שבת

phrases.english: This is the principle:
anyone who does a forbidden labor,
and his work lasts on Shabbat — is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the general principle behind the cases listed in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability depends on the מלאכה being lasting (מתקיימת).

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: striking the anvil also counts
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that even a smith who strikes his sledgehammer on the anvil during work is חייב, because it is like improving the work.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: even one who strikes with a sledgehammer on the anvil during his work is liable, because he is like one who improves the work.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds one more case to the list. A craftsman who taps the anvil while working is also liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hitting the anvil does not directly shape the metal. Still, it helps prepare and smooth the work, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל treats it as part of the מלאכה. This stretches the idea of 'contributing to the work' further than the earlier cases.

keyTerms.meaning: Like one who improves or prepares the work

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: And similarly, Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
even one who strikes with a sledgehammer on the anvil
during his work — is liable,
because he is like one who improves the work.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another case that fits the principle of contributing to the work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Striking the anvil during work makes one liable, because it helps the work along.

steps.title: What use is a tiny bit of building?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what purpose a tiny building could serve that would make it a real מלאכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Any amount — what is it fit for?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question about the משנה's ruling. It is setting up the next moves, where the אמוראים will look for a useful tiny building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מלאכה must be meaningful and useful, and it must have a parallel in the work of the משכן. So the גמרא wants a real case where a very small building is still useful, both in daily life and in the משכן.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it fit for? What use does it have?

steps.confusionAlert: This is not an attack on the משנה. The גמרא accepts the ruling and is only looking for a realistic example that explains it.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Any amount — for what is it fit?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: A practical use for a tiny amount of building, with a parallel in the משכן.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: a small hole to hide coins or needles
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה answers that a poor man digs a small hole to hide his coins. In the משכן, the curtain-sewers dug holes to hide their needles.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Because a poor man digs a hole to hide his coins in it. Its parallel in the משכן: the curtain-sewers dug a hole to hide their needles in it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה gives the first answer. He offers a tiny building that is useful in ordinary life and has a parallel in the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Digging a small hole in the floor of a house counts as building. A poor man finds even a tiny hole useful for storing coins. To make it a real מלאכה, רבי ירמיה matches it to the משכן, where the sewers of the curtains supposedly hid their needles in such holes.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
because a poor man digs a hole
to hide his coins in it.
Its parallel in the Tabernacle:
the sewers of the curtains dug a hole
to hide their needles in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A small hole to hide coins, which parallels the curtain-sewers hiding needles in the משכן.

steps.title: אביי: needles rust, so they would not do that
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רבי ירמיה's משכן parallel: needles rust in the ground, so the sewers never hid them that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Since they rust, they would not do so.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבי ירמיה's answer. He says the case from the משכן is not realistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי does not argue with the daily-life case of the poor man. He attacks only the משכן side: no one would bury needles in the ground, because they would rust. Without a real משכן parallel, the example fails.

keyTerms.meaning: They do not do it this way

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Since they rust, they would not do so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר כֵּיוָן דְּמִשַּׁתְּכִי לָא עָבְדִי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the משכן parallel offered in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the משכן half of רבי ירמיה's example.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Needles buried in the ground would rust, so the sewers would not have done this.

steps.title: אביי's answer: legs for a small stove
steps.stepSummary: אביי offers a new case: a poor man builds legs for a small stove to hold a small pot. In the משכן, the dye-cookers built a small stove to finish a small amount of dyeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because a poor man makes legs for a small stove to set a small pot on it. Its parallel in the משכן: those who cooked herbs to dye curtains whose dyeing was lacking a bit would make legs for a small stove to set a small cauldron on it.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבי ירמיה, אביי gives his own example of a useful tiny building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Building small legs or supports for a stove is a small act of building. A poor man needs only a tiny stove for a tiny pot. In the משכן, when only a little more dye was needed to finish the curtains, the dyers would supposedly build a small stove for a small pot instead of a big one.

keyTerms.meaning: Small legs or supports for a stove
To set a pot on the fire
Whose work was lacking a little

phrases.english: Rather, because a poor man makes
legs for a small stove
to set a small pot on it.
Its parallel in the Tabernacle:
those who cooked herbs to dye curtains
whose work was lacking a little,
would make legs for a small stove
to set a small cauldron on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שֶׁכֵּן עָנִי עוֹשֶׂה פִּיטְפּוּטֵי כִּירָה קְטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבי ירמיה's rejected example with a new one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Building legs for a small stove, which parallels the dyers in the משכן finishing a small amount of dye.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב: no poverty in a place of wealth
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב rejects אביי's משכן parallel: the משכן was a wealthy project, and they did not work in a stingy, small-scale way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: There is no poverty in a place of wealth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב pushes back on אביי's example. He says the משכן would never use a small, 'poor man's' stove.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משכן had plenty of resources, so the workers would simply cook the dye in a full-size pot even if only a little was needed. This removes the משכן parallel for אביי's case, just as אביי removed the parallel for רבי ירמיה's.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no poverty in a place of wealth

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Yaakov said:
There is no poverty in a place of wealth.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר אֵין עֲנִיּוּת בִּמְקוֹם עֲשִׁירוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects אביי's משכן parallel from step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The משכן half of אביי's example.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wealthy משכן would not use small, poor-style equipment.

steps.title: רב אחא's answer: sealing a small hole
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב gives the final example: a homeowner seals a small hole in his house. In the משכן, a worm-bored hole in a beam was sealed with poured lead.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, because a homeowner who has a hole in his house seals it. Its parallel in the משכן: a beam that a worm attacked — one pours lead into it and seals it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב offers his own example of a useful tiny building. This is the last answer, and it stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This example does not depend on being poor, so 'no poverty in a place of wealth' does not knock it down. Even a rich owner fixes a small hole, and even the משכן would fill a small worm hole in a beam. Sealing a small hole is a useful act of building at any size.

keyTerms.meaning: A worm that bores into wood

steps.whatToRemember: Building even a tiny amount is a real מלאכה, because sealing a small hole is useful to anyone, rich or poor. Its משכן parallel is filling a worm hole in a beam with lead.

phrases.english: Rather, because a homeowner
who has a hole in his house seals it,
Its parallel in the Tabernacle:
a beam that a worm attacked —
one pours lead into it and seals it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, שֶׁכֵּן בַּעַל הַבַּיִת שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ נֶקֶב בְּבִירָתוֹ וְסוֹתְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces אביי's rejected example with one that does not depend on poverty.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sealing a small hole in a house, which parallels sealing a worm hole in a משכן beam with lead.

steps.title: שמואל: setting a stone in place is building
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that one who sets a stone in place on שבת is liable for building.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: One who sets a stone in place is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. שמואל rules that placing a building stone in position, even without mortar, counts as בונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, the act of fixing the stone in its spot is enough for building. He does not require mortar to bind it.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sets or positions (a stone) in place

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
One who sets a stone in place — is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל הַמְצַדֵּד אֶת הָאֶבֶן חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about what counts as building.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting a stone in place, without mortar, is enough for liability for בונה.

steps.title: Challenge: only the one who adds mortar is liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from a ברייתא: when one person places the stone and another adds the mortar, only the one who adds the mortar is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: If one places the stone and one places the mortar — the one who places the mortar is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling with a teaching that seems to say otherwise.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, the person who only set the stone is not called liable; only the one who added the mortar is. This suggests that placing a stone alone is not building, which contradicts שמואל.
steps.confusionAlert: The challenge comes from what the ברייתא leaves out: it calls only the mortar-placer liable, which implies the stone-placer is not.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
one places the stone
and one places the mortar —
the one who places the mortar is liable!

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, אֶחָד נוֹתֵן אֶת הָאֶבֶן וְאֶחָד נוֹתֵן אֶת הַטִּיט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that setting a stone in place is enough for liability.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes only the mortar-placer liable, which implies that setting the stone alone is not building.

steps.title: Your reading has a problem too: רבי יוסי makes placing alone liable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to the end of the same source, where רבי יוסי says placing a stone on a top row is enough for liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, look at the last part: רבי יוסי says that even if he lifted a stone and placed it on top of a row of stones, he is liable!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge from step 11. It shows that even the questioner's own source says simply placing a stone can make you liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that placing a stone without mortar never counts as building. רבי יוסי says placing a stone on a top row does make you liable. So 'placing never counts' cannot be the full rule, and the next step will explain the real rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning (turning the question back on the asker)
The latter clause of a source
A row of stones in a wall

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
say the latter clause:
Rabbi Yosei says:
and even if he lifted and placed
on top of a row of stones
he is liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends שמואל against the ברייתא brought in step 11 by showing the source cannot mean that placing never counts.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Counter-reading (ליטעמיך): the same source contains a case where placing alone makes one liable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Placing a stone without mortar is never building.
steps.terutzMaskana: Placing can be building in some cases, so the rule needs to be refined.

steps.title: Three kinds of rows, each with its own requirement
steps.stepSummary: Building has three levels. The bottom row needs the stones set in with dirt, the middle row also needs mortar, and the top row needs only placement.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, there are three kinds of building: bottom, middle, and top. The bottom row needs the stones set in place with dirt. The middle row also needs mortar. The top row is done by simply placing the stone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real rule. What counts as 'building' depends on which row of the wall you are working on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each source was talking about a different row. שמואל's מצדד is about the bottom row, where setting the stone firmly into the ground with dirt (צדודי ועפרא) is the building, with no mortar needed. The ברייתא that requires mortar is about a middle row. רבי יוסי is about the top row, where placing alone finishes the building. So the challenge against שמואל is answered.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether placing a stone counts as בונה depends on the row. On the bottom row (שמואל's case), setting the stone firmly with dirt is building. On the middle row, it is not building until mortar is added. On the top row (רבי יוסי's case), placing alone is building.

phrases.english: Rather, there are three kinds of building:
bottom, middle, and top.
The bottom requires setting and dirt.
The middle requires mortar as well.
The top is done with mere placement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the resolution that step 12 pointed toward.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case distinction (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different row
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא requiring mortar contradicts שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a middle row, which needs mortar. שמואל is about the bottom row, where setting the stone firmly with dirt is building. רבי יוסי is about the top row, where mere placement is building.

steps.title: Which מלאכה does a chiseler violate?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of chiseling and asks which category of מלאכה it falls under.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And one who chisels.' One who chisels, for which מלאכה is he liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic from the משנה, the chiseler (מסתת). It asks which אב מלאכה his act belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a chiseler is liable but does not say which מלאכה he violates. Chiseling could be seen as part of building, or as the final touch that finishes an object.

keyTerms.meaning: One who chisels or dresses a stone

phrases.english: And one who chisels.
One who chisels, for what is he liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new piece of the משנה. The building-a-row discussion has ended.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which אב מלאכה makes the chiseler liable.

steps.title: רב says building, שמואל says the final hammer blow
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that chiseling is בונה. שמואל holds that it is מכה בפטיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: because of building. And שמואל said: because of striking with a hammer.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered with a disagreement. רב puts chiseling under בונה, and שמואל puts it under מכה בפטיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the chiseler is liable. They argue only about which category the act belongs to. מכה בפטיש is the מלאכה of giving the final touch that completes an object.

keyTerms.meaning: Striking with a hammer: the final act that completes a vessel or object

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think one of them says the chiseler is exempt. Both agree he is liable. They only argue about which מלאכה he violates.

phrases.english: Rav said: due to building,
and Shmuel said: due to striking with a hammer.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם בּוֹנֶה, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם מַכֶּה בַּפַּטִּישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14 with a מחלוקת.

steps.title: The same disagreement in two more cases: a coop hole and a hoe pin
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל argue the same way about making a hole in a chicken coop and about putting a pin into a hoe handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who makes a hole in a chicken coop: רב said it is building, and שמואל said it is striking with a hammer. One who puts a pin into the handle of a hoe: רב said it is building, and שמואל said it is striking with a hammer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists two more cases where רב and שמואל argue in exactly the same way. This sets up the question of why all three cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case רב says בונה and שמואל says מכה בפטיש. Because the pattern repeats, a reader would wonder why the גמרא did not just teach one case. The next steps answer that.

phrases.english: One who makes a hole in a chicken coop,
Rav said: due to building,
and Shmuel said: due to striking with a hammer.
One who inserts a pin into the handle of a hoe,
Rav said: due to building,
and Shmuel said: due to striking with a hammer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same מחלוקת from step 15 to two more cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In both the coop-hole case and the hoe-pin case, רב says בונה and שמואל says מכה בפטיש.

steps.title: Why the coop case is needed after the chiseling case
steps.stepSummary: From chiseling alone, we might think רב says בונה only because chiseling is normal building work. For a coop hole, which is not normal building, we might think he agrees with שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is necessary. Had we been taught only the first case, I would say רב said building there because that is the normal way of building. But making a hole in a chicken coop is not the normal way of building, so I would say רב agrees with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a צריכא, explaining why each case teaches something new. Here it shows why the coop case adds to the chiseling case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chiseling stones is a regular part of building, so רב's view there might not reach further. A hole in a coop is not typical building. Teaching that case shows that רב calls it בונה anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (to teach every case)
This is the normal way of building

phrases.english: And it is necessary,
for had it taught us only the first case,
in that case Rav says (building),
because that is the normal way of building.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל עוֹשֶׂה נֶקֶב בְּלוּל שֶׁל תַּרְנְגוֹלִים,
phrases.english: But one who makes a hole in a chicken coop,
which is not the normal way of building,
I would say he agrees with Shmuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the repeated disputes in step 16 are not redundant.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case adds a new piece of information
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב's view applies only to typical building work like chiseling.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב says בונה even for a coop hole, which is not typical building.

steps.title: Why the hoe-pin case is needed after the coop case
steps.stepSummary: A coop hole resembles building because it works like a window for air. A pin in a hoe handle looks nothing like building, so we might think רב agrees with שמואל there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And had we been taught only this case, I would say רב said building here because it is similar to building, since the hole is made for ventilation. But a pin in a hoe handle is not the normal way of building, so I would say רב agrees with שמואל.
steps.whatsHappening: The צריכא continues. The גמרא shows why the hoe-pin case teaches something about רב that the coop case did not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ventilation hole is like a window in a house, so it still looks somewhat like building. Fixing a tool handle does not look like building at all. Teaching this case shows how far רב extends בונה, even to fixing a tool.

phrases.english: And had it taught us only this case,
in this case Rav says (building),
because it resembles building,
since he makes it for ventilation.
But a pin in the handle of a hoe,
which is not the normal way of building,
I would say he agrees with Shmuel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָא — בְּהָא קָאָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the צריכא, moving from the coop case to the hoe-pin case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב says בונה only where the act resembles building, like a ventilation hole.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב says בונה even for fixing a pin in a tool handle.

steps.title: From שמואל's side, the other two cases are needed, so all three are necessary
steps.stepSummary: From the hoe-pin case alone, we might think שמואל says מכה בפטיש only there, and agrees with רב on chiseling and the coop. So all three cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And had we been taught only this case, I would say שמואל said striking with a hammer here. But in those other two cases, I would say he agrees with רב. So it is necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the צריכא by looking at שמואל's side. It concludes that all three disagreements had to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each case is chosen to show how far one opinion goes. The chiseling and coop cases show שמואל holds מכה בפטיש even where the act looks like building. The hoe-pin case shows רב holds בונה even where the act does not look like building.
steps.whatToRemember: רב and שמואל keep their views in all three cases. Chiseling and the coop hole show how far שמואל goes, and the hoe pin shows how far רב goes. That is why all three cases are needed.

phrases.english: And had it taught us only this case,
in this case Shmuel says (striking with a hammer),
but in those two cases,
I would say he agrees with Rav.
It is necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בְּהָא, בְּהָא קָאָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא from שמואל's side and closes the section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three disagreements are needed. They show that רב holds בונה and שמואל holds מכה בפטיש in every one of these cases.

steps.title: רב נתן בר אושעיא asks רבי יוחנן about chiseling
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אושעיא asks רבי יוחנן which מלאכה one is חייב for when chiseling a stone.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר אושעיא asked רבי יוחנן: someone who chisels a stone on שבת, for which מלאכה is he חייב?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a question put to another אמורא, רבי יוחנן, about the same issue רב and שמואל argued over: chiseling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already saw that רב says chiseling is בונה (building) and שמואל says it is מכה בפטיש (the final hammer blow). Now someone asks רבי יוחנן directly, so we can see which side he takes.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question, not an attack)
One who chisels or smooths a stone

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב נָתָן בַּר אוֹשַׁעְיָא
phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Oshaya asked
of Rabbi Yochanan:
One who chisels, for what is he liable?
phrases.notes: Asks which main category (אב מלאכה) applies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new voice (רבי יוחנן) into the רב/שמואל dispute about chiseling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether chiseling is חייב under בונה or under מכה בפטיש.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן gestures: it is striking with a hammer
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers with a hand motion that chiseling is מכה בפטיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: He showed him with his hand: it is because of מכה בפטיש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers, not in words but with a hand motion, that chiseling falls under מכה בפטיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer matches שמואל's view, not רב's. Chiseling is seen as the final finishing touch on the stone, and finishing touches belong to מכה בפטיש.

keyTerms.meaning: He showed him with his hand (answered by gesture)
Striking with a hammer, the final finishing blow that completes an item

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the hand motion is a separate opinion. It is simply his answer, given by gesture instead of words: מכה בפטיש.

phrases.english: He showed him with his hand
because of striking with a hammer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Chiseling is חייב because of מכה בפטיש, like שמואל.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה lists chiseling and hammer-striking separately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה says 'the chiseler AND the hammer-striker,' which sounds like two different things.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: 'One who chisels and one who strikes with a hammer'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי יוחנן's answer from the wording of a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'and' (ו) in the משנה makes chiseling and מכה בפטיש look like two separate items on the list. If chiseling were itself מכה בפטיש, why would the משנה list them separately?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)? A challenge from a source
And the one who strikes, where the 'and' suggests a separate item

phrases.english: But didn't we learn (in the Mishnah):
One who chisels and one who strikes with a hammer!
phrases.notes: Notice the word 'and': it makes it sound like these are two separate categories.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that chiseling is מכה בפטיש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lists them with 'and,' implying they are two different things, so chiseling cannot be מכה בפטיש.

steps.title: Answer: read the משנה as one item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא re-reads the משנה without the 'and': 'the chiseler, who is a מכה בפטיש.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'One who chisels, a striker with a hammer.' Meaning, the chiseler is חייב because of מכה בפטיש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by changing how we read the משנה, dropping the 'and.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'and' removed, the משנה no longer lists two items. It explains that the chiseler is a type of מכה בפטיש, which fits רבי יוחנן exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read it this way), an emendation or re-reading of the text

phrases.english: Say: One who chisels, (is) one who strikes with a hammer.
phrases.notes: The 'and' (ו) is removed, so it reads as one category.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation / re-reading of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists chiseling and מכה בפטיש as two separate מלאכות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה describes chiseling as a form of מכה בפטיש, so it fits רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: Come and hear: a proof is about to be brought
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with 'תא שמע' to bring a source that will help settle the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear (a source):
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote a source as a proof, and the source itself comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'תא שמע' always introduces a source that should help decide the open question, here which מלאכה chiseling is. Nothing is proven yet. Wait for the quoted text.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Transitions from the emendation to bringing a proof on the question of chiseling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A source quoted on the next amud.
